title: Learning Theory Lab
description: A finite hypothesis class, a known data distribution, and a direct comparison between empirical risk and a uniform-convergence bound.
question: How quickly does the gap between empirical and population risk decrease as the sample grows?
method: Compare 41 fixed threshold classifiers on a synthetic distribution with independent label noise. Compute each classifier’s exact population risk, then repeat sampling 128 times at each training-set size.
limitation: The plotted trial percentiles are descriptive Monte Carlo statistics. They are not confidence intervals, and the probability guarantee applies separately at each sample size.
note_title: A finite-class generalization bound, one step at a time

summary.interpretation: Synthetic Monte Carlo illustration; percentile band is not a confidence interval.

title: Convex Optimization Notes
description: Gradient descent and Nesterov acceleration on the same quadratic, with known curvature and an exact reference solution.
question: What changes when momentum uses known smoothness and strong-convexity constants?
method: Construct one positive-definite 24-dimensional quadratic with condition number 50. Start both methods at zero and compare their objective gaps over 200 gradient steps.
limitation: This experiment uses exact curvature constants and a single synthetic objective. It does not establish which optimizer is best for neural-network training.
note_title: What a quadratic can teach us about momentum

summary.interpretation: One synthetic quadratic with known curvature constants; no neural-network claim.

title: Information Extraction Lab
description: A transparent baseline for finding entity mentions and relations in text, with explicit annotations and exact-match evaluation.
question: Which entity mentions and relations can a small rule-based baseline recover, and how should its errors be counted?
method: Run a fixed gazetteer and relation-pattern baseline on 12 independently annotated synthetic examples. Compare entity spans, types, relation direction, and endpoints using micro exact-match precision, recall, and F1.
limitation: The fixture was created alongside the baseline for explanation and testing. It is not a held-out benchmark. Unseen names and unsupported paraphrases expose known failure cases; the scores do not establish generalization.
note_title: From a sentence to entities, relations, and evidence

summary.dataset: 12 hand-authored synthetic examples, including known failure cases
summary.evaluation: Micro exact-match precision, recall and F1; half-open character offsets
summary.limitations: Illustrative fixture designed alongside the baseline; not a held-out benchmark. No generalization claim.
